# truncate

Set the length of regular files using supported filesystem operations.

## Usage

```sh
moonx cli/truncate -s 0 notes.txt
moonx cli/truncate -c -s 1M data.bin
```

## Common options

<!-- BEGIN GENERATED OPTIONS -->
<!-- Generated by tools/metadata from options.json. -->

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `-s VALUE`, `--size VALUE` | Set a size or apply a signed adjustment. |
| `-c`, `--no-create` | Skip a missing file. |
| `--help` | Show help. |
| `--version` | Show the version. |
| `-r VALUE`, `--reference VALUE` | Use the length of a regular reference file. |
<!-- END GENERATED OPTIONS -->

## Notes

Zeroing and creation use filesystem open modes. Positive sizes can create or extend a regular file by writing its last byte. Shrinking an existing file to a nonzero size requires handle truncation. Growth requires exclusive access to the file while adjusting its length.

See the [compatibility guide](../../docs/compatibility.md).
